return: The canonical base -2 representation as an ASCII string of 0/1 digits with no leading zero, except that zero returns "0". Digit position i contributes digit*(-2)^i.
mutation_aliasing: Only scalar inputs are read. A private digit container is built least-significant first and reversed/joined; the returned string has no mutable input alias. The Solution instance retains no state; separate calls share no mutable result state.
numeric: At each step choose the unique remainder in {0,1} for which value-remainder is divisible by -2. Python nonnegative modulo already provides it; JavaScript explicitly normalizes its possibly negative remainder. All values/subtractions have magnitude at most n+1 <= 1000000001 and the quotient is an exactly representable integer. JavaScript may internally compute -0 at termination; it compares equal to 0 and never appears as an output digit. At most 33 digits suffice on this domain.
